subject: Commercial options for air‑gapped on‑prem deployment — fee split & support lifecycle
messages:
From: Tony Alvarez <tony@aureliahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurelia Health Procurement <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: on‑prem pricing breakdown for air‑gapped runbook

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Procurement asked me to capture a couple of concrete items so they can start internal approvals:

- We need a clear split between the one‑time licensing/seat/node fee and the platform fee (amortized vs upfront) for an air‑gapped on‑prem deployment.
- Any additional surcharge you apply specifically for air‑gapped installs (e.g., support logistics, secure image delivery).
- Support tiers: what’s included in Standard vs. Enterprise for on‑prem (SLA, on‑call, RTO, remote patching allowances).
- Migration/implementation credits for a three‑year commit — does Redwood offer credits against platform fee or engineering retainer?

Can you send an options document we can attach to the purchase request? Also flag any items that require an exceptions path (paperwork, shipment schedule) in your standard SOW.

I attached our internal timeline (see procurement). Ideally we’d lock terms this month.

—Tony
Director, AI Engineering
Aurelia Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tony Alvarez <tony@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: on‑prem pricing breakdown for air‑gapped runbook

Tony — thanks, appreciate the clarity. I’ll pull together a short options pack that splits: licensing (per node), platform fee (monthly or amortized), and the air‑gap surcharge line items. I’ll also include suggested support tiers and an example SOW addendum for air‑gapped delivery.

I’m looping in Aditya (pricing) and Marissa (commercial/SOW) so we can run the options by procurement and propose an optimal amortization scenario for your finance team. Expect a draft by EOD Monday.

Quick Q — are you evaluating a 3yr commit for capacity (we’ll show 1yr/3yr)? And do you anticipate on‑site engineering during install or fully remote packaging?

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0112

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tony Alvarez <tony@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick: on‑prem pricing breakdown for air‑gapped runbook

Team — forwarding Tony’s ask. High level requirements: air‑gapped on‑prem for a healthcare customer, likely 3yr commit but show 1yr/3yr. Procurement wants: license vs platform fee split, explicit air‑gap surcharges, support tier mapping, and migration/implementation credit options.

Key constraints: they will likely require secure image delivery and limited ship schedule windows for on‑site work (if any). Please draft 2 commercial options:

Option A (Conservative):
- One‑time license per node (list price).
- Platform fee: paid upfront year‑by‑year, optional amortization over 36 months.
- Air‑gap surcharge: 8% of total platform fee to cover secure packaging + offline delivery + expedited engineering slots.
- Standard Support: 24x5 email & ticket SLA (24h initial response), Enterprise adds 24x7 on‑call and 4‑hour P1 response.

Option B (Aggressive — for committed customers):
- Discounted license per node (15% off) for 3yr commit.
- Platform fee: amortize across the commit (show 12/36 mo amortization).
- Air‑gap surcharge: waived for 3yr committed deals but subject to a modest implementation retainer.
- Migration credit: $50k credit applied against platform fee for > $1M ARR commit.

Please include an example SOW addendum that lists deliverables (secure image handoff, transfer checklist, acceptance tests, rollback plan) and a short note on documentation/audit support (SOC2 artifact packaging allowed on secure media). Attach the pricing workbook and SOW template.

—Olga

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick: on‑prem pricing breakdown for air‑gapped runbook

Folks — draft spreadsheet attached (airgap_pricing_options_v1.xlsx). High‑level numbers below (examples for 10 node cluster):

- List license: $180k one‑time (per node $18k)
- Platform fee (run): $12k/month (unamortized) → $432k over 3 years
- Air‑gap surcharge (Option A): 8% of platform fee = ~$34.6k one‑time admin/packaging fee
- Option B (3yr commit): license 15% off → $153k, platform fee amortized → show as $12k/month but apply 12% committed discount to platform fee for year 1; implementation retainer $30k, migration credit up to $50k applied at signing for >$1M net ARR.

Notes:
- For indemnity/compliance-heavy installs we push on a higher engineering retainer to cover additional validation cycles (we can show a $25–50k band).
- If they insist on amortizing platform fee for accounting, we can offer a quoted amortization schedule (12/24/36 months) with internal finance signoff.
- Margin impacts: Option B reduces gross margin by ~6–8 points; need revenue commit to secure.

I added a tab that maps support tiers to SLAs and included sample language for the SOW deliverables.

—Aditya
Sr. Pricing & Commercial Analyst | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tony Alvarez <tony@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick: on‑prem pricing breakdown for air‑gapped runbook

Adding commercial/SOW perspective:

- SOW: include explicit acceptance criteria and an offline artifact handoff checklist. We should add a 30‑day post‑install warranty window (remote only) and a separate optional on‑site commissioning day rate.
- Platform fee amortization: recommend we show both invoice options (annual prepaid vs. monthly amortized via internal financing) and call out the tax/finance implications in the cover note — this helps procurement pick the right line in their CAPEX/OPEX review.
- Air‑gap surcharge approach: prefer to present a waived surcharge for 3yr commit (with $30k retainer) vs. a one‑time managed packaging fee for short commits. That gives procurement a clear tradeoff.
- Doc signs: put primary contract in DocuSign and SOW as an attachment; procurement likes having the SOW as a separate exhibit.

I’ve attached the redwood_sow_template_v2.docx and added suggested exhibit language in the workbook. Happy to draft the doc package to send to Tony after you both sign off on numbers.

—Marissa
Sr. Commercial Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Tony Alvarez <tony@aureliahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: on‑prem pricing breakdown for air‑gapped runbook

Team — this is perfect, thank you. Procurement will review the two options (A/B) and the SOW exhibits tomorrow. A couple of clarifications we’ll likely ask for:

- Can you convert the amortized platform fee into an annualized line for our CAPEX request? (If you show both, that’s ideal.)
- On the waived surcharge for the 3yr commit: procurement needs the retention/exit language spelled out (what happens if we reduce capacity year 2).
- We will need a certified shipping window noted in the SOW for air‑gap media handoffs — suggest we mark it as 7–10 business days by default.

If you can send the final package (pricing workbook + SOW + example DocuSign envelope) by EOD Tuesday we can start approvals on Wednesday.

Appreciate the speed — talk soon.

—Tony
Director, AI Engineering | Aurelia Health
